messages:
maya: heads-up — after the recent kernel selection change (flash_attn_v2 -> cuda_fwd_attn_v2) I'm seeing an uptick in P90 RTF and more soft 429s from the front-end. small thread with profiling + quick experiment ideas.

rajesh: saw that in the nightly perf runs. p50 looks fine but p90 jumped ~28% on gpus with long sequences (seqlen>1024). aggregate metrics: p50=18ms, p90=54ms, p99=120ms for generate path. KV hit rate unchanged.

lina: do we know whether the batch formation changed? if kernel latency variance increases, continuous-batcher might wait longer to fill minibatches -> larger batch sizes -> more tail latency.

maya: exactly my hypothesis. KV cache behavior is weird too — when KV hits are high we still end up coalescing requests into bigger batches. suspect the batch timer heuristics + token-budget calc are not accounting for new kernel jitter.

sam: quick profiler dump I ran on a repro pod:
```
# sample timeline (seqlen 1500, batch window 8-12ms)
kernel_select: cuda_fwd_attn_v2 (chosen)
batch_assemble: 9ms
kernel_enqueue: 2ms
kernel_exec: median 11ms, p95 72ms (spikes)
kv_apply: 1ms
post_process: 3ms
```
Those p95 spikes line up with the p90 RTF bump.

rajesh: kernel selection fallback picked cuda_fwd for a subset because it had better avg throughput in microbenchmarks, but it has higher variance on long contexts. flash_attn had slightly worse avg but better tail. we didn't surface tail metrics in selection scoring.

lina: two levers: (1) change kernel scoring to include tail percentiles (p90/p95) so we prefer lower-variance kernels for tail-sensitive routes, (2) make admission control KV-aware and token-budget conservative when variance high.

maya: +1 on both. Also propose a short-term soft limit tweak: lower the token_budget target by 15% for the next canary to reduce batch sizes and keep latency SLOs while we adjust kernel scoring.

sam: proposed experiment config (A/B):
```
experiment: gentle-throttle-admit-v1
routes: [chat-short, chat-long]
admit_policy:
  mode: probabilistic_preempt
  token_budget_target: 0.85  # baseline is 1.0
  kv_priority: true
  dropout_prob: 0.12  # randomly shed 12% when queue depth > 120
kernel_score:
  weights: {avg:0.4, p90:0.4, mem:0.2}
```
This keeps most traffic but reduces batch inflation.

lina: for KV priority: prefer admitting requests with KV hit by a factor of 1.3 in the token budget accounting. So token charge = tokens * (kv_hit ? 0.7 : 1.0). That should bias accept toward faster responses.

rajesh: we should also add a quick telemetry dimension: kernel_choice + kernel_latency_percentile + batch_size histogram per route. then auto-rollback if p95 latency regresses >10% vs baseline for >5m.

ops-bot: incident-bot: alert created #INC-5563 — spike in soft 429s on prod-us-west-2 between 05:12-05:18 UTC.

maya: thanks. ops, can you hold a short canary rollout to 5% for gentle-throttle-admit-v1? want to monitor request success, p90, KV-hit acceptance delta.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary config queued. deploying to subset=5% in prod-us-west-2 now.

sam: quick note — keep the continuous-batcher window logic unchanged for the first canary; just adjust token_budget_target and the probabilistic_preempt params. this isolates variables (kernel scoring change is separate experiment).

lina: agreed. also add an experiment that toggles kernel scoring to include p95 for a follow-up if the admit changes don't fully recover tail.

rajesh: one more safety: while canary is live, if 429 rate > baseline + 0.8% absolute for 3 consecutive minutes, auto-fallback to baseline token_budget_target=1.0 and disable dropout.

maya: sounds good. i'll own telemetry dashboard cards and the postmortem if things go sideways.

sam: I'll wire the config and push the canary. attaching the patch diff shortly.

maya: thanks team — follow-ups: (1) deploy canary 5% (sam) (2) dashboards + automated rollback (rajesh + maya) (3) kernel scoring follow-up experiment plan (lina). check back in 30m for initial signals. :thumbsup:
